newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on KNP BT Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on KNP BT Q4 results.

text.p: Dutch paper, packaging and office products group KNP BT said on Wednesday its fourth quarter net profit from ordinary operations fell to 92 million guilders from 151 million in the same period of 1995.

The company said it expected a "material improvement" in earnings from ordinary operations in 1997 but it was uncertain whether paper prices would continue to recover this year after a slight rise in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on the results.

"Firstly, it's in line with my expectations. However, I was a little surprised by the good paper result in the fourth quarter and I'm very hopeful for 1997. Packaging is pretty good. They sold part of it without losing any operating profit. For next year, we see an increase in the price of paper and expect no increase in pulp prices, although that's mainly for the second half of the year."

"It's a bit of a mixed picture, the bottom line was a bit disappointing although the fourth quarter operating profit was satisfactory, especially at KNP Leykam where the operating profit was higher than expected at 26 million guilders."

"More down the line I think the tax rate was relatively high at 30 percent. All in all, operationally it looks good but bottom line was about 10 million short of my estimates," he said. Verstoep added he had been looking for fourth quarter net profit after extraordinary items of over 100 million.
